keeps.why: The current pin 45.4101,-84.9050 is on neither campground: Esri imagery there shows houses and tennis courts in the private wooded subdivision north of the park road, just west of M-119, ~0.8 km NNE of the Dunes loop. The Dunes sites (OSM camp_site way 997605816, 45.4022-45.4053 / -84.9108 to -84.9092; DNR campground map loop of sites 1-80) sit at the edge of the open dunes south of the day-use beach house; 45.4037,-84.9099 is on that loop's road at its central junction (sites 40/41/80). Elevation 188 m is Open-Meteo at the new pin (the stored 199 m was the wrong spot's).

adds.name: Petoskey State Park - Tannery Creek Campground
adds.note: The larger of Petoskey State Park's two campgrounds, at the park's south end about 1 km south of the Dunes Campground at the end of its own spur of the park road. Wooded loops behind a low foredune on Little Traverse Bay, with boardwalks from the loop ends to the beach; the bike trail to Petoskey leaves from the south end. --Claude
adds.inclusion_evidence: michigan.gov/recsearch/parks/petoskey (read 2026-10-25): 'Petoskey Tannery Creek Modern Campground ... paved pads at each site. All sites have 20- and 30-amp service, and a handful of sites have 50-amp service', 'Number of sites: 98', reservable at 800-447-2757 or online; MiDNRReservations (Petoskey State Park, resourceLocationId -2147483532, map 'Tannery Creek', read 2026-10-25): 98 campsites + 2 mini cabins; allowed equipment 'Trailer or RV up to 40'' at 6 sites, 35' at 9, 30' at 13, 25' at 41, 20' at 28, tents only at 1 (69 sites take 25 ft or more); posted site lengths 27-60 ft; every site 'Pull Through=No' (the DNR page's 'Pull-through sites available' tag is not borne out by the booking site).
adds.waterfront_evidence: Esri World Imagery (Vantor WV02 0.5 m, 2023-05-29) on an EPSG:3857 frame at 45.3950,-84.9132 + USGS 3DEP 1 m lidar (epqs) transects 45.3941-45.3962 + DNR campground map ('boardwalk to beach' off the west loop ends): the loops sit in the shore forest at ~180-181 m, 4 m above the bay (176.4 m), behind a low wooded/grassy foredune (crest ~181-182 m) and a ~15-20 m natural beach; nearest drive-in pads are the south loop's west end (sites 164-167), ~45-55 m from the waterline (loop-road tip ~36 m), the northern loop ends ~65-75 m back under canopy. No road, parking, day-use or cabin strip between (the day-use beach is ~1.3 km north); the apron is part-treed and at or past the ~50 m bound, so not bayfront -> coastal woods (Great Lake shore forest).

separation: Site loops ~0.65 km apart (Dunes loop's south end 45.4022 to Tannery Creek's north loop 45.3965); pins ~1.0 km apart. Both are reached through the park's single entrance and contact station off M-119; the park road passes the Dunes Campground entrance and continues ~0.8 km south through forest to Tannery Creek, whose loops hang off their own spine road at the end of it (DNR park map; OSM; Esri imagery). Separate campgrounds with separate roads and their own toilet/shower buildings, but a shared park entrance and somewhat under the ~1 km guide.
